about.title: Personal Injury Help in Cudahy, California
about.longDescription: Cudahy is a small, tightly packed city in Los Angeles County, and its streets carry a lot of daily traffic through residential blocks. Public records for the most recent full year show 34 injury collisions and 51 people injured on Cudahy streets, with no traffic deaths reported. Crashes here tend to cluster on Fridays between 4 and 6 p.m., often along corridors like Atlantic Avenue, Clara Street, Wilcox Avenue, and Santa Ana Street — busy routes that see a steady mix of cars, pedestrians, and cyclists. If you were hurt in one of these incidents, the paperwork and insurance calls that follow can feel like a second job on top of recovering physically. We handle personal injury claims for Cudahy residents — working on contingency means there's no fee unless you recover money. Reaching out costs nothing and doesn't commit you to anything; it's simply a way to find out where you stand.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Cudahy Claim

items.title: Two Years to Act, But Don't Wait
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury claim. If a government entity or vehicle was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months, so it pays to get informed early.

items.title: Shared Fault Doesn't Shut You Out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning even if you were partly responsible for the crash, you can still recover damages — just reduced by your share of fault.

items.title: No Ceiling on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain, suffering, and loss of enjoyment of life.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Unless You Win
items.desc: We work on contingency, so there's no upfront cost and no fee unless your case results in a recovery.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in Cudahy?
items.answer: In most cases, California law gives you two years from the date of the injury to file a claim. If your injury involves a government vehicle or property, that deadline can be as short as six months, so it's worth checking your situation sooner rather than later.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to happen in Cudahy?
items.answer: Based on public crash records, collisions in Cudahy tend to cluster along Atlantic Avenue, Clara Street, Wilcox Avenue, and Santa Ana Street, with the most reports typically occurring on Fridays between 4 and 6 p.m. These are simply the corridors with the highest recorded collision counts, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, which means you can still recover compensation even if you shared some responsibility for the crash. Your recovery would just be reduced by the percentage of fault assigned to you.

items.question: Does it cost anything to contact your team?
items.answer: No. Our initial consultation is free. If you move forward with us, we work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover money.

items.question: Is there a limit on how much I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: In standard California personal injury cases, there is no cap on non-economic damages such as pain and suffering. The specific amount depends on the facts of your case, which we can help evaluate.
